problem: The equation y′ + P√y = Q does not become linear under u = √y. Substituting y = u² gives 2u u′ + P u = Q, which still contains u u′, so it is not of the form u′ + P u = Q. A student following this bullet gets stuck. The error is that the f′(y) factor required by the template f′(y)y′ + P f(y) = Q has been left out of the stated equation.
fix: Write the equation in template form for f(y) = √y: y′/(2√y) + P√y = Q. With u = √y, u′ = y′/(2√y), so it becomes u′ + P u = Q, which is linear in u. State plainly that y′ + P√y = Q itself is not linearizable this way.

problem: The same missing factor: y′ + P ln y = Q does not become linear under u = ln y. Since y = e^u and y′ = e^u u′, the equation becomes e^u u′ + P u = Q, i.e. u′ + P u e^(−u) = Q e^(−u), which is nonlinear in u. The bullet's claim that it reduces to u′ + P u = Q is false.
fix: Write the equation in template form for f(y) = ln y (y > 0): y′/y + P ln y = Q. With u = ln y, u′ = y′/y, so it becomes u′ + P u = Q, linear in u.
